title: Learning to Predict by the Methods of Temporal Differences
summary: Richard S. Sutton published 'Learning to Predict by the Methods of Temporal Differences' in Machine Learning in 1988. The paper introduces a class of incremental prediction-learning procedures that assign credit using differences between temporally successive predictions and studies convergence and optimality in special cases.
significance: A documented reinforcement-learning research milestone establishing temporal-difference methods in the peer-reviewed literature.

verification.note: The 1988 Machine Learning paper itself and its bibliographic records establish Richard S. Sutton as author, volume 3 pages 9-44, DOI 10.1007/BF00115009, and the paper's stated introduction of incremental prediction-learning procedures based on differences between temporally successive predictions. LINEAiGE preserves year precision only because the evidence used in this admission run does not justify treating any more specific date as the authoritative publication milestone. No organization, geography, ancestry, influence, causality, or relationship is inferred.
